Demote the semantic-union iff to a preliminary gluing lemma. Replace the current existential strict-extension claim by the following explicit, vertex-minimal witness for the excluded regime of two adjacent singleton clusters on a feasible directed cycle.

Let the binary observed vertices be V={a,b,c,d}, with known clusters K_a={a}, K_b={b}, K_cd={c,d}. Let H have precisely the directed cluster edges K_a→K_b, K_a→K_cd, K_cd→K_a, K_b→K_cd, K_cd→K_b, and no bidirected edges. Thus K_a→K_b→K_cd→K_a is a directed cycle containing adjacent singleton clusters.

Two exact acyclic refinements are G1={c→a,c→b,a→b,a→d,b→d}, with topological order c,a,b,d, and G2={d→a,d→b,a→b,a→c,b→c}, with topological order d,a,b,c. Both coarsen exactly to H. Their common skeleton is K4 minus {c-d}, and neither has an unshielded collider, so they have the same positive observational model, characterized by c ⟂ d | (a,b).

Define a strictly positive binary law by p(c=1)=1/2; p(a=1|c=0)=1/4 and p(a=1|c=1)=3/4; [p(b=1|a,c)]_(a,c)=((1/8,3/8),(5/8,7/8)); and [p(d=1|a,b)]_(a,b)=((1/5,2/5),(3/5,4/5)), with complementary probabilities for value zero. The same law factorizes over G2, with p(d=1)=1/2; [p(a=1|d)]_(d=0,1)=(19/80,61/80); [p(b=1|a,d)]_(a,d)=((9/61,6/19),(13/19,52/61)); and [p(c=1|a,b)]_(a,b)=((5/26,1/2),(1/2,21/26)). For EX={K_a}, EY={K_b}, Pr_G1(b=1|do(a=0))=1/4 and Pr_G2(b=1|do(a=0))=537/2318; Pr_G1(b=1|do(a=1))=3/4 and Pr_G2(b=1|do(a=1))=1781/2318. The differences are respectively 85/4636 and -85/4636. Open-neighborhood rank zero implies that the derivative of Ftilde_S vanishes in every simplex-tangent direction throughout connected U0, so Ftilde_S is locally constant there. Consequently the singleton region covers on E_N, and its asymptotic coverage is 1, not 1-alpha.
